gaps.sentence: Sorry I am late — I ___ to take my car to the garage this morning.
gaps.explanation: Past obligation uses 'had to', since 'must' has no past form: had to.

gaps.sentence: When I was a child, I ___ stay up late on New Year's Eve.
gaps.hint: permission that existed in the past
gaps.explanation: 'Was allowed to' expresses past permission; 'could' is also possible: was allowed to.

gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ to leave the gallery by 6 p.m.
gaps.hint: have to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' takes the full infinitive with 'to': have to leave.

gaps.sentence: He ___ be hungry — he has just eaten a three-course meal.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' rules out the possibility based on evidence: can't be hungry.

gaps.sentence: You ___ have seen her face when she heard the news!
gaps.explanation: 'Should have seen' emphasizes how remarkable something was: should have.

gaps.sentence: I'm afraid you ___ smoke anywhere in the terminal; it is strictly forbidden.
This bill ___ be right — we only ordered two coffees.
gaps.hint: an obvious mistake, so it is impossible
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' shows the speaker believes something is not possible: can't be right.

gaps.sentence: Her car is not in the car park and her office light is off, so she ___ home.
gaps.hint: a confident conclusion about the past
gaps.explanation: A confident conclusion about the past uses 'must have' plus the participle: must have gone.
